about: The collecta of the formulary “Easter Sunday” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: God, today You opened the way to eternity for us through Your Only-Begotten Son, after death had been conquered. You first inspire our desires. Sustain them also with Your help. Through the same Jesus Christ, our Lord, Your Son, who, as God, lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit forever and ever.

a.g: opened for us the entrance to eternity, death having been conquered
also sustain with Your help our desires, which You first inspire in us
the same Jesus Christ, our Lord, Your Son

ex.w013: Devicta morte is an ablative absolute: “death having been conquered”.
ex.w021: Praeveniendo describes God’s initiative in inspiring our desires. Adiuvando describes His continuing help.
